gaps.sentence: Don't phone between seven and eight — we ___ dinner then.
gaps.hint: in progress at a stated future time
gaps.explanation: Something in progress at a stated future time takes the future continuous: will be having.

gaps.sentence: By the time I woke up, my flatmates ___ to work.
gaps.hint: by the time plus past simple
gaps.explanation: 'By the time' plus a past action refers back to an earlier past action, so the past perfect is needed: had gone.

gaps.sentence: My grandfather ___ walk five miles to school when he was a boy.
gaps.hint: a past habit no longer true
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' describes past habits or states that are no longer true: used to walk.

gaps.sentence: The audience always ___ when the curtain falls.
gaps.explanation: 'Always' marks a general habit, which takes the present simple: claps.

gaps.sentence: The soup ___ delicious, but I think it needs a little more salt.
gaps.hint: taste describing a quality is stative
gaps.explanation: When 'taste' describes a quality of something, it is a state verb: tastes.

gaps.sentence: While the chef ___ the sauce, the waiter set the tables.
gaps.hint: while frames the longer simultaneous action
gaps.explanation: 'While' frames the longer simultaneous action, which takes the past continuous: was preparing.

gaps.sentence: We ___ to Greece for our honeymoon, but that was twenty years ago.
gaps.hint: twenty years ago fixes a finished past
gaps.explanation: A finished time expression like 'twenty years ago' demands the past simple: went.

gaps.sentence: There ___ a cinema on this corner, but it closed years ago.
gaps.hint: a past state that has ended
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' is also used for past states that no longer exist: used to be.
